title: 2021 Fall AMC 10B Problem 18
statement:
Three identical square sheets of paper each with side length \(6\) are stacked on top of each other. The middle sheet is rotated clockwise \(30^\circ\) about its center and the top sheet is rotated clockwise \(60^\circ\) about its center, resulting in the \(24\)-sided polygon shown in the figure below.

The area of this polygon can be expressed in the form \(a-b\sqrt{c},\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are positive integers, and \(c\) is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(a+b+c?\)

solutions.text:
The boundary can be split into \(24\) congruent triangles. Each has angles \(15^\circ,\) \(45^\circ,\) and \(120^\circ.\)

For one such triangle, draw the altitude from the center-side direction. The altitude is \(3,\) half the side length of a square. The adjacent right triangle has a \(30^\circ\) angle, so the part cut off from a length \(3\) base is \(3\tan30^\circ=\sqrt3.\)

Thus each small triangle has base \(3-\sqrt3\) and height \(3,\) giving area \(\frac{3(3-\sqrt3)}{2}=\frac{9-3\sqrt3}{2}.\)

The total area is \[24\cdot\frac{9-3\sqrt3}{2}=108-36\sqrt3.\] Hence \(a+b+c=108+36+3=147.\)

Thus, the answer is E .
hints: Split the polygon into \(24\) congruent triangles
